attempts.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) to route between lan-a (node2, 10.50.10.0/24 via eth1) and lan-b (node3, 10.50.20.0/24 via eth2) with no NAT so original source addresses are preserved. Added VyOS forward-filter accept rules for both directions plus established/related state, added static routes to the peer subnet on node2/node3 (via NetworkManager static profiles on their second NIC, since NM's DHCP reconciler was wiping raw `ip addr`/`ip route` changes), and opened firewalld with rich rules on node2/node3 permitting all traffic from the peer LAN so any port is reachable directly. Verified with ping, arbitrary-port TCP (python http.server) in both directions, and tcpdump on node1's both interfaces confirming source IPs are unchanged end-to-end. All three nodes were then restarted one at a time (safe reboot, quorum/independent-node concerns N/A here since this is not a clustered service), each showed a changed boot_id post-restart, and all config (VyOS interfaces/firewall, NM static route, firewalld rich rule) and connectivity were confirmed recovered after each restart.
